knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Circulation of a Vector Field Over a Region Containing Holes

question.:question/problem:
![](/media/jake/SSD/EDB/math/generators/34/346dcfcfb54e4ac2b1f35d8f710b0d88c871653f5ec3fa647f2c6a805c8662d4/source-assets/images/ef/efc1df0808af7ab4dacfb3031fdde2132bceaf0e89f88788110d7b5f5ed688bf.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=5,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-1,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-5,
$$

where ${C}_{1}$ is oriented counterclockwise and ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ are oriented clockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/media/jake/SSD/EDB/math/generators/34/346dcfcfb54e4ac2b1f35d8f710b0d88c871653f5ec3fa647f2c6a805c8662d4/source-assets/images/f7/f7869b25194e311c08df6c5b647fe9c53f7064c94eaa5d60fa1fa2551a6b58a1.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =5+(-1)+(-5) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
